reconstructed_theorem_text:
For every complete finite-dimensional real inner-product space E with its Borel measurable structure, consider a twice continuously Frechet differentiable V:E->R and a nonnegative real kappa>=1 such that, for all x,v in E,
  kappa^(-1)||v||^2 <= D^2 V(x)[v,v] <= ||v||^2.
Choose eta,epsilon in R with 0<eta<1 and epsilon>0, J in N with J>=2, and h in R with h>0. Index exactly J nodes by Fin(J)={0,...,J-1}. Define
  t_i=(h/2)(1-cos((i/(J-1))pi)),
  ell_j(X)=product_{k in Fin(J),k!=j} (t_j-t_k)^(-1)(X-t_k),
  Lambda=sup{sum_j |ell_j(s)| : s in [0,h]},
  omega_ij=integral_0^{t_i} (t_i-s)ell_j(s) ds,
  pw_j=omega_{J-1,j},
  bw_j=integral_0^h ell_j(s) ds.
The node quotient is real, the ell_j are real polynomials, Lambda is the real supremum of the displayed closed-interval image, and the oriented interval integrals use real Lebesgue measure. Assume additionally the exact smallness inequality h^2 Lambda<=1.
Then there exist measurable p,q:E->E and N:E->N satisfying, simultaneously for every y in E,
  p(y)+eta grad V(p(y))=y,
  ||q(y)-p(y)||<=epsilon,
  proximalQuery(grad V,eta,epsilon,y,N(y)+1,y)=some(q(y),N(y)+1),
and p is nonexpansive: ||p(u)-p(v)||<=||u-v|| for every u,v in E.
The actual interpreter proximalQuery(g,eta,epsilon,y,fuel,x) fails with none at zero fuel. At fuel n+1 it evaluates g(x), sets z=y-eta g(x), and tests
  ||z-x|| <= (1-eta)epsilon.
If this test passes, it returns some(x,1); otherwise it recursively calls the same interpreter with anchor y, iterate z and fuel n, propagates failure and adds one to a successful returned count. Equivalently it compares ||x+eta g(x)-y|| to (1-eta)epsilon. The successful terminal gradient/residual test is counted. The value N(y)+1 in the theorem is an adequate finite execution certificate and its exact reported count; it is not a promise that the count certificate is computed before the run without cost.
Let G be the centered identity-covariance Gaussian probability measure on E and define
  gamma=(G x G) x ((product_{Fin(J)} G) x (product_{Fin(J)} G)).
All four factors are independent: two Gaussian vectors and two arrays with J independent Gaussian vector coordinates each. For f:E->E and w=((X,P),((zeta0,zeta1),(G0,G1))), define the phase map by
  a=exp(-h/2), sigma=sqrt(1-exp(-h)),
  P0=a P+sigma zeta0,
  Y0_i=X+t_i P0,
  Z0_j=grad V(f(Y0_j)+sqrt(eta)G0_j),
  Y1_i=Y0_i-sum_j omega_ij Z0_j,
  Z1_j=grad V(f(Y1_j)+sqrt(eta)G1_j),
  Phi_f(w)=(X+h P0-sum_j pw_j Z1_j,
            a(P0-sum_j bw_j Z1_j)+sigma zeta1).
All sums use the entire Fin(J) index set. On the state space S=E x E use the explicit distance
  d2((X,P),(Xprime,Pprime))=sqrt(||X-Xprime||^2+||P-Pprime||^2).
This is the stated square-root sum-of-squares distance, without identifying it with the default product-space norm. For real rho and measures mu,nu on S, define
  W_rho(mu,nu)=[inf_{tau measure on S x S: tau.fst=mu,tau.snd=nu}
                  integral^- (ENNReal.ofReal(d2(s,sprime)))^rho dtau(s,sprime)]^(rho^(-1)).
Here the integral is the lower integral, the infimum is over all coupling measures with precisely those marginals, and the cost and root powers are real powers in extended nonnegative reals. ENNReal.ofReal is the extended-nonnegative embedding of max(value,0).
There exist Markov kernels Kp,Kq:S->S with probability outputs such that, for every incoming state s,
  Kp(s)=(z -> Phi_p(s,z))_* gamma,
  Kq(s)=(z -> Phi_q(s,z))_* gamma,
and, for every incoming state s and every real rho>=1,
  W_rho(Kq(s),Kp(s)) <= ENNReal.ofReal(3 h Lambda epsilon).
The exponent rho is an arbitrary real at least one, including noninteger values and with no upper bound.
For the same chosen p and Kp there is also this general perturbation conclusion: for every measurable r:E->E, every real delta>=0 and every uniform approximation condition ||r(y)-p(y)||<=delta for all y, there exists a Markov kernel Kr:S->S with probability outputs satisfying for every state s
  Kr(s)=(z -> Phi_r(s,z))_* gamma,
and for every state s and every real rho>=1,
  W_rho(Kr(s),Kp(s)) <= ENNReal.ofReal(3 h Lambda delta).
Each kernel works simultaneously for all states and all specified exponents. The comparison uses the same incoming state on both sides. No input state distribution or finite-moment assumption is part of this theorem. Its conclusions do not assert optimal-coupling attainment, sampler invariance or convergence, a contraction between distinct incoming states, a total phase-evaluation bound, or machine-precision behavior.
objects: The real inner-product space E; potential V, its gradient and Hessian quadratic form, kappa; eta,epsilon,J,h; exactly J cosine nodes t,Lagrange basis ell,interval supremum Lambda,integrated omega and weights pw,bw; global measurable p,q,N; actual recursive proximalQuery; independent Gaussian noise law gamma; phase map Phi_f; state space E x E and explicit d2 distance; coupling lower-integral infimum and extended-nonnegative W_rho; Markov kernels Kp,Kq; arbitrary measurable perturbation r with uniform error delta and its kernel Kr.
